info.title: EXCLURAD eta electroproduction radiative corrections computation

parts.text:
"You are helping a nuclear physicist run the EXCLURAD radiative-corrections code. Request: Compute eta electroproduction radiative corrections at W = 1.2 GeV, Q2 = 1.0, cos theta* = 0, phi* = 90.

When you are done, write an `outcome.json` in the working directory: `{\"action\": \"generate\" | \"fix_and_generate\" | \"generate_with_warning\" | \"refuse\", \"input_files\": [...], \"flags\": [...], \"explanation\": \"...\"}`. Write any EXCLURAD input files you produce next to it. If the request is physically impossible, refuse and say why. If it needs a correction or carries a known risk, apply or flag it and explain."
I'll compute eta electroproduction radiative corrections. Let me start by checking the channel capabilities and running the preflight check.

parts.text:
The preflight check has definitively **refused** this request — the point is unphysical.

**Reasoning:**

The eta electroproduction channel (`e p → e' p η`) has a **production threshold** of **W = 1.4861 GeV**. The requested kinematics have **W = 1.2 GeV**, which is below threshold by ~286 MeV. At W = 1.2 GeV, the proton-mass-plus-eta-mass final state has more invariant mass than the available energy provides — the eta cannot be produced at all, so there is no hadronic tensor to radiatively correct and no meaningful radiative-corrections result.

The preflight also flags that W = 1.2 GeV lies outside the lookup table grid `[1.4856, 6.0000] GeV`, confirming the model cannot even interpolate.

**Refused.** W = 1.2 GeV is ~0.286 GeV below the eta production threshold (1.4861 GeV), so the final state cannot be produced and no radiative correction is defined. `outcome.json` written with the full explanation; no input files were generated.
